conclusion: Bit 8 remains the owner-bound control and admission/retire contract. CP26 adds bit 9 (GENERIC_EXECUTION_V2) only with bit 8 and all dependencies, and the locked daemon trace proves the causal GPUDispatcher/ComputeUnit path rather than treating a type-20 control response as execution evidence.
decision: Keep bit 8 and bit 9 as separate negotiated capabilities. Require the exact 5528-byte zero-preload gpuReadWrite fixture, ordered daemon trace, independent A/B/C D2H oracle, nonzero output CRC, and no CPU/NVIDIA fallback before asserting execution. Preserve bit-8-only output_crc32c=0 and fail closed for arbitrary gfx950, preload-aware Triton images, and incomplete capability sets.
invalidated_assumptions: A bit-8/type-20 control lifecycle by itself proves GPUDispatcher or ComputeUnit execution.
A nonzero client-reported CRC without a daemon trace and independent D2H oracle proves kernel output.
Bit 9 may be selected without bit 8 and topology, queue, memory, signal, and code-object dependencies.
The locked fixture result generalizes to arbitrary gfx950 HSACO or Triton preload images.
observation: The accepted live route selects bits 8 and 9, issues only the hash-pinned zero-preload gpuReadWrite image, and records fetch=1, command-processor submission=1, four workgroups, sixteen waves, 304 instruction starts, 1024 reads, 2048 writes, 32 stores, and the exact A/B/C oracle. Bit-8-only completion remains CRC zero while bit 9 emits CRC32C 0x6f67026f.
question_or_symptom: Why must the exact GPU execution gate use a separate bit 9 instead of treating CP25 bit 8 and type 20 as execution evidence?
